# Export-InstalledSoftware

Exports an inventory of installed software (name, version, publisher, install date) to CSV.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Changes the system** | No, read-only |
| **Supports `-WhatIf` / `-Confirm`** | Not needed (read-only) |
| **Admin rights** | No |
| **PowerShell** | Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+ |
| **Source** | [scripts/Export-InstalledSoftware.ps1](https://github.com/lucaswsanchez/helpdesk-kb/blob/main/scripts/Export-InstalledSoftware.ps1) &middot; [tests](https://github.com/lucaswsanchez/helpdesk-kb/blob/main/tests/Export-InstalledSoftware.Tests.ps1) |

## Description

Reads the Windows "Uninstall" registry keys, the same source used by "Apps & features", for 64-bit, 32-bit and per-user applications. System components and updates/patches are excluded, and duplicate entries are removed.

Useful for license audits, checking whether an approved application is installed, or comparing two computers when "it works on my colleague's PC". The script only reads the registry; it changes nothing.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-OutputPath` | String |  | Path of the CSV file to create. Defaults to .\InstalledSoftware_<COMPUTER>_<yyyyMMdd>.csv in the current folder. |
| `-RegistryPath` | String[] | `@( 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall', 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall', 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall' )` | Registry paths to read. Defaults to the standard machine (64/32-bit) and current-user Uninstall keys. Mainly useful for testing. |
| `-NameFilter` | String | `'*'` | Optional wildcard filter on the application name, for example '*Office*'. |
| `-PassThru` | switch |  | Also return the inventory objects to the pipeline. |

## Examples

```powershell
.\Export-InstalledSoftware.ps1
```

Writes InstalledSoftware_<COMPUTER>_<date>.csv in the current folder.

```powershell
.\Export-InstalledSoftware.ps1 -NameFilter '*Adobe*' -PassThru | Format-Table Name, Version
```

Shows installed Adobe products and also writes the CSV.

## Notes

Works on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+. No admin rights needed. Related KB: KB-016 Install Approved Software from Company Portal.
